lines.text: The harbor at last: wet planks, tarred boats, and Jonas's upturned hull fifty steps away. The smell of warm bread drifts across the quay.

lines.speaker: teun
lines.text: We made it! Look, Pip, we made it, and I only drummed twice! ...Three times.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Fifty steps. I could walk fifty steps in my sleep.]
Two flashlights click on behind them. The color drains from the planks as Sergeant Hush and Officer Mute step out from behind the fish carts.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Section 9, Subsection Hush. Unlicensed percussion within a hundred paces of a harbor building. Stand where you are.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Decibel reading, one hundred and four. Sergeant, the file said the boy was cheerful. It did not say how cheerful.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Fifty steps, and two flashlights between us and the door. We are not going to get there together.]

lines.speaker: teun
lines.text: Pip. Count to ten, then go for Jonas's door. Don't look back.

lines.speaker: teun
lines.text: Somebody has to be loud so somebody else can be quiet. Ma Ruby taught me that.
Teun walks out into the light, lifts his sticks, and plays the loudest, happiest rhythm of his life.

lines.speaker: hush
lines.text: Cease that. Cease. Officer Mute, the restraints.
The beams swing away from Pip and follow the drum. He slides along the wall and through Jonas's door. Behind him the rhythm stops in the middle of a beat.

lines.speaker: jonas
lines.text: Sit down, son, and keep away from the window. They will want something for that boy now. Names, most likely. Yours, mine, anyone who ever played a note.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [He drummed so I could stay quiet. I will never be able to say that out loud.]
